transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Leah Ortiz (Redwood Solutions), Jordan Miles (Anemone Head of ML), Priya Nair (Eng Manager), Marcus Li (Infra Lead), Nina (Anemone note taker)

Summary (auto-gen, may be imperfect):
Anemone is evaluating migrating from OpenAI-hosted endpoints to Redwood Dedicated (possible private deployment). Main drivers: cost predictability, latency for batch+streaming, evaluation parity with our current Anthropic/OpenAI models, and enterprise security (SOC2, VPC). They run vLLM in-house for some workloads and use TGI for others; compatibility and API parity are top concerns. Next steps agreed: pricing, SOC2 docs, and a benchmarking session.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. I'm Alex from Redwood, this is Samir, our solutions engineer, and Leah on solutions. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Jordan (Anemone): Good, thanks. We just grabbed coffee. Excited to dig in — we want to understand the migration story from OpenAI to Redwood Dedicated and if we can keep eval parity.
[00:17] Samir (SE): Great. Quick agenda I sent earlier — current stack, pain points, throughput & latency targets, security requirements, and then we can talk deployment options: hosted, dedicated, private VPC.
[00:27] Priya (Customer): Sounds good. Quick intro: we run production chat + semantic search. Most generation is via OpenAI gpt-4 style endpoints; embeddings for search. For latency-critical flows we batch, and we also run vLLM for some internal workloads.
[00:40] Marcus (Infra): We have about 1.1M tokens/day now; spikes up to 5x during peak. 90th p99 latency target for assistant flows is 300ms token latency, ideally lower. Costs are a problem — tokens are eating into our margin.
[00:54] Alex: Thanks. On cost — Dedicated typically reduces unit cost via reserved capacity and better batching. We also have quantized variants and caching that lower per-token compute. Curious — how tied are you to the exact OpenAI model outputs? Is model parity strict or is eval-based parity OK?
[01:12] Jordan: Eval parity is key. Our compliance team requires we don't regress on intent extraction and hallucination metrics. We have a 40-prompt eval suite. If you can show identical or better scores, that's a win.
[01:24] Samir: Totally. We usually run a head-to-head on your eval set — same prompts, same temp/top-p, and measure BLEU/ROUGE style metrics plus custom classifiers. Note that open models and quantization can shift behavior; we mitigate with fine-tuning or prompt shim layers.
[01:40] Priya: How do you handle vLLM / TGI compatibility? We have some teams that run vLLM locally against GGML quantized models; others call TGI endpoints. Migration friction here is a concern.
[01:50] Samir: Good question. Redwood Dedicated supports multiple runtimes — we have a vLLM-compatible execution path and also run TGI-style containerized runtimes for certain models. API-wise, we provide the same generation primitives and can proxy your existing calls with minimal client-side change. Sometimes tokens and stop behavior differ slightly — we've built a shim and a small adapter layer to reproduce OpenAI stop sequences.
[02:12] Marcus: Network wise — can we run Dedicated in our VPC? We need private network connectivity and key management.
[02:18] Leah: Yes. We offer Dedicated with a private control plane and can do VPC peering or private link. For Private (on-prem/VPC), customers can bring KMS or integrate HSM; we support SSO/SAML and audit logs. We'll share our network diagram.
[02:32] Jordan: Okay. On eval parity — you mentioned quantization might change outputs. Our legal compliance is pretty strict about data residency. If we do Private, can we keep everything in our cloud account and have Redwood manage the control plane?
[02:44] Alex: Yes — our Private deployment options include a customer-managed VPC with the control plane either in Redwood but with private connectivity, or fully customer-hosted in some enterprise cases. We can lock logs and retention and integrate with your KMS.
[02:57] Priya: What about throughput? We need steady 200 tokens/sec sustained across 10 parallel assistant sessions during peak. How does Dedicated handle autoscaling and burst?
[03:08] Samir: Dedicated has reserved GPU pools and configurable autoscaling policies. For bursts, you can provision burst capacity or reserve extra nodes. We can model the steady throughput to recommend pool sizes; also continuous batching and KV cache reduce load for repeated prefixes.
[03:23] Marcus: Are there known regressions when moving from GPT-4-ish endpoints to open models you're hosting? For example hallucination increase or longer prompts causing perf issues.
[03:33] Samir: There can be differences. We run eval parity tests during onboarding. If needed, we recommend a small supervised fine-tune or a prompt engineering layer to match behavior. Also quantization levels trade cost vs quality; we can show perf numbers for int8/int4 for your workload.
[03:51] Jordan: What's typical onboarding length for a Dedicated pilot? We want a two-week POC ideally.
[03:57] Alex: Two-week POC is common: first week for setup and benchmarks, second week for tuning and running your eval suite. We'll run comparisons against OpenAI and document deltas.
[04:07] Priya: If we run internal vLLM and then route to Redwood for scale, is there a hybrid pattern?
[04:13] Samir: Yep. Many customers run local inference for high-sensitivity or tiny models, and route scale/production traffic to Redwood with routing policies. Our API supports model aliasing so you can A/B traffic to local vs Redwood endpoints.
[04:25] Nina (Anemone): (whisper) can you show the latency numbers you mentioned earlier?
[04:29] Alex: We'll include a latency spreadsheet. For similar-sized models on A100-class hardware with optimization we typically see tail token latencies in the 120-250ms range depending on sequence length and batching. But again, depends on model and quantization.
[04:44] Marcus: Security checklist — SOC2, ISO, SAML, RBAC, audit logs, KMS, data deletion policies. We also need pen-test evidence.
[04:53] Leah: We have SOC2 docs and ISO attestation; we'll share redacted pen-test summary and our audit log schemas. For SSO we support SAML and OIDC, role-based controls, and single-tenant log retention.
[05:06] Jordan: Pricing — can you walk through the Dedicated pricing model? We currently pay OpenAI per token but want predictability.
[05:12] Alex: Dedicated is subscription for reserved capacity plus a variable usage if you exceed. We'll send a worksheet with different pool sizes and projected cost. Typically customers see 30-60% reduction in per-token compute costs but trade upfront commit. We'll model it for your 1.1M tokens/day baseline and spike patterns.
[05:29] Priya: One more on eval parity — do you support function-calling and structured outputs? Our assistants rely on tool calling to downstream services.
[05:38] Samir: Yes — function/tool calling is supported, we also have streaming and structured output helpers. We can simulate your tool-calling flows in the benchmark.
[05:47] Jordan: Any customers that ran this exact migration from OpenAI to Redwood? Case studies?
[05:52] Alex: We have a mid-market PLG company that moved to Dedicated — we can share an anonymized case study and some benchmark numbers. We'll include that in the follow-up.
[06:02] Marcus: For the POC, what do you need from us?
[06:05] Samir: Sample prompts (your eval suite), representative traffic patterns, and a sample dataset for embeddings if you want search parity. Also, infra details for VPC peering if we do private.
[06:15] Priya: Timeframe — we want to decide by end of month (two weeks). Is that feasible?
[06:20] Alex: Yes, if you can share the eval and metrics this week we'll do the bench next week and have results before your deadline.
[06:28] Jordan: Cool. Let's recap. Action items: Redwood sends pricing + SOC2 + network diagram; Samir sets up benchmarking plan; Anemone shares eval prompts and infra metrics; schedule a benchmark meeting.
[06:39] Alex: Correct. Anything else?
[06:42] Nina: One tiny question — are there limitations on model uploads or private model hosting? We have a small fine-tuned policy model currently.
[06:49] Leah: We support private model hosting in Dedicated; you can upload custom weights, or we can host variants. We'll check licensing for certain vendor models but fine-tuned customer models are supported.
[06:59] Jordan: Great. Thanks everyone.
[07:02] Alex: Thanks, talk soon.

End of transcript.
